question:
**Medical Science – Tumor Localization**

An imaging device at $(10,-6,12)$ reflects across plane $4x-y+5z=8$.

(1) Find coordinates of the image.

(2) Obtain equation of line joining device and image.

(3) Find length of segment from device to plane.

(4) Explain how this reflection helps tumor mapping.
explanation:
Normal vector $(4,-1,5)$.

Using normal-line method gives foot $F(0.667,-3.667,0.333)$.

Image point $(-8.666,-1.334,-11.334)$.

Line through device and image: $(10,-6,12)+\lambda(-18.666,4.666,-23.334)$.

Distance from point to plane $=\frac{|4*10+6+60-8|}{\sqrt{42}}=\frac{98}{\sqrt{42}}\approx15.12$.

Reflection enables accurate mirrored localization of structures in scans.

options.A:
(1) Image point is $\left(\frac{2}{3},-\frac{11}{3},\frac{1}{3}\right)$
(2) Joining line is $(10,-6,12)+\lambda(4,-1,5)$
(3) Length from device to plane is $\frac{49}{\sqrt{42}}$
(4) It identifies only the foot of perpendicular
options.B:
(1) Image point is $\left(-\frac{26}{3},-\frac{4}{3},-\frac{34}{3}\right)$, approximately $(-8.666,-1.334,-11.334)$
(2) Joining line is $(10,-6,12)+\lambda\left(-\frac{56}{3},\frac{14}{3},-\frac{70}{3}\right)$
(3) Length from device to plane is $\frac{98}{\sqrt{42}}\approx15.12$
(4) Reflection enables accurate mirrored localization of structures in scans
options.C:
(1) Image point is $\left(\frac{26}{3},\frac{4}{3},\frac{34}{3}\right)$
(2) Joining line is $(10,-6,12)+\lambda\left(\frac{56}{3},-\frac{14}{3},\frac{70}{3}\right)$
(3) Length from device to plane is $\frac{42}{98}$
(4) Reflection gives the plane normal only
options.D:
(1) Image point is $(10,-6,12)$
(2) Joining line is undefined
(3) Length from device to plane is $0$
(4) The device already lies on the plane
